biography.plain_text: Eugénia Grandchamp des Raux is a French photographer whose work explores movement, ritual and collective celebration. Her 2014 book Danse drew on close access to Paris Opera dancers, while later projects examined festivals from Rio and Venice to Seville and Mexico. The Maison Européenne de la Photographie presented her Momentos Cariocas series in 2018.

long_biography.plain_text:
Grandchamp des Raux came to photography after practising figure skating and dance, experiences that shaped her attention to bodies in motion. Working with performers from the Paris Opera, she used deliberate blur and unusual framing to suggest rhythm rather than freeze it. The resulting photographs became Danse, a 256-page bilingual volume published in 2014.

Her lens also followed public ceremonies and popular gatherings across several countries: Holy Week in Seville, Venetian and Rio carnivals, Saint-Tropez traditions and Mexico's Day of the Dead. Paris's MEP later showed Momentos Cariocas, a colour-rich study of the Rio carnival. A 2025 exhibition in Sant Antoni, Ibiza, returned to dance, underscoring the subject's lasting place in her work.
